Q189.L1t: Procedural due process under the Fourteenth Amendment governs when a state must give notice and a hearing before it deprives a person of a protected interest.
Q189.L2t: Professional licenses that a person has already obtained are generally treated as protected property or liberty interests, so states may not revoke them without due process.
Q189.L3t: Due process requires a hearing only to resolve disputed facts, and here the conviction in a prior criminal trial with full procedural protections already established the facts that triggered the mandatory revocation.
Q189.L4t: The board can revoke the license without a further hearing because the criminal trial already determined the relevant facts, so a trial-type hearing would serve no purpose.
Q189.L2f: A medical license is only a revocable privilege, so the state may take it away at any time without any procedural protections.
Q189.L3f: The Constitution's full faith and credit clause requires every agency of a state to treat a state court judgment as binding, so a licensing board has no discretion to hold its own proceeding after a conviction.
Q189.L4f: The board should win because the full faith and credit clause obliges it to give effect to the conviction and revoke the license summarily.

Q190.L1t: The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination and the Miranda rules limit how police may obtain statements from people suspected of crimes.
Q190.L2t: The prosecution must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that a confession was voluntary before it can be admitted at trial.
Q190.L3t: Under due process, a confession obtained by coercion, threats, or other overbearing of the suspect's will is not the product of free choice and cannot be used as evidence.
Q190.L4t: A confession is inadmissible when the statement was involuntary.
Q190.L2f: Under current law, a confession is treated as voluntary and admissible so long as the suspect was physically unharmed, whatever other pressure police used.
Q190.L3f: Miranda protections apply only to statements made in response to police questioning, so a statement that was not a response to known interrogation is not admissible, whatever the circumstances.
Q190.L4f: A confession is inadmissible when it was not made in response to a known police interrogation.

Q191.L1t: Partnership law determines when people doing business together share responsibility for the business's debts to outsiders.
Q191.L2t: A lender who receives only repayment of a loan, with interest not measured by profits, is generally not a partner in the borrower's business.
Q191.L3t: A person who represents himself, or permits himself to be represented, as a partner is liable to any third party who extends credit in reasonable reliance on that representation.
Q191.L4t: Both Bob and Ted are liable to Pete, jointly, because Ted is a partner by estoppel.
Q191.L2f: A lender who accepts a reduced interest rate on a loan thereby becomes a co-owner of the business under partnership law.
Q191.L3f: A business operated under a partnership name creates a distinct legal entity, so the third-party creditor's claims are limited to the assets of that business and not those of the individuals.
Q191.L4f: Pete can recover only from the de facto partnership arising from the Wilson and Lamar relationship, and not from either man personally.
